name: create_location
description: Add a new location to the campaign. Use it when the story reaches a place that does not exist yet. Names must be unique among locations and NPCs. Set discovered to true only when anyone in the world would have heard of the place, so the player already knows it. To put a place inside another, give parent set to the name of that top-level location; such a place has no map point of its own, so leave out x and y.

description.description: What the place looks, sounds, and smells like, in a sentence or two.

discovered.description: True if the player already knows the place, because it is famous or the story has revealed it. False by default.

x.description: Kilometers east of the map's center; negative for west. Give x and y together, or neither to leave the place off the map. Only when the place's position relative to others is known; do not use 0 as a default.

y.description: Kilometers north of the map's center; negative for south. Give x and y together, or neither. Only when the place's position relative to others is known.

force.description: Set true only to put this place on a point another place already has, as when two places are the same spot. Without it, a point another place already has is refused.

parent.description: The name of the top-level location this place is inside. Leave it out for a place on the map. A place with a parent cannot be given x or y.

name: create_npc
description: Add an NPC to the campaign and place them at an existing location. Leave personality, accent, or quirks out to have them generated at random; give them only when the story calls for a specific trait. Give character options, such as appearance or biography, only when the story calls for them; anything left out is rolled or left blank. A name that matches a published statblock, such as a creature in the module, takes that statblock's stats, armor, and attacks, so leave the stats out of the character options. For an NPC with no statblock, set hp_tier to the tier their role in the story calls for. Names must be unique among locations and NPCs.

location.description: The name of the location the NPC is at. It must already exist.

description.description: Who the NPC is: appearance, role, and what they are doing.

personality.description: Optional. How the NPC carries themselves.

accent.description: Optional. How the NPC sounds when they speak.

quirks.description: Optional. Habits or mannerisms the NPC shows.

force.description: Set true only to create a custom NPC under the name of a published statblock. Without it, such a name is refused if stats are given.

name: move_actor
description: Move the player character or an NPC to another existing location. Use it when someone travels or is sent somewhere. Travel follows the routes in the location descriptions: send the player character only to a place reached by a route from where they are, and never to a place they have not heard of, unless something forces them there (a trap, a teleporter, or a spell). A forced move discovers the place on arrival. The player character starts unplaced, so on the first turn create the place where the story begins and move the player character there. Moving the player character to a place discovers it. Leave location out to send an NPC into the wind: it is at no location until a later move brings it back. The player character cannot go into the wind.

name.description: The name of the player character or of the NPC who moves.

location.description: The name of the location to move them to. It must already exist. Omit it only to send an NPC into the wind.

name: add_note
description: Record a note for yourself as the GM, to track events, updates, and situations so you stay consistent. It is not written for the player. Attach it to a location or NPC by giving its name as the subject; leave the subject out for a note about the campaign as a whole. The result includes the note's id, for later update_note or delete_note calls.

text.description: The fact to remember, written as a complete sentence.

subject.description: Optional. The name of the location or NPC the note is about.

name: search_notes
description: Search your GM notes on events, updates, and situations, to stay consistent. Every word in the query must appear in the note's text or in its subject's name. Each result includes the note's id. Use it before continuing a thread or answering questions about what has happened before.

name: all_at_location
description: Look up a location: its description, the NPCs there (with personality, accent, and quirks), whether the player character is there, and the notes about the place or those NPCs. Leave out the location to look at the player character's current location. Use it whenever you need to know what is in a place before you narrate it or act in it.

location.description: The location's name. Leave it out for the player character's location.

name: search_location
description: Find locations by words in their name or description. Every word in the query must appear. Use it to find a place you have described before or to check whether a place already exists before you create one.

name: search_npc
description: Find NPCs anywhere in the world by words in their name, location, description, personality, accent, or quirks. Every word in the query must appear. Each result gives the NPC's location. Use it to check whether an NPC already exists before you create one, or to find someone the story mentions.

name: get_statblock
description: Get a character's statblock: stats, template, features, and fields. Works for the player character and for NPCs. Statblocks are not in your context until you fetch them, so fetch one before a roll, before a change to a character's abilities or gear, or whenever their capabilities matter to the outcome.

name: character_options
description: List the values a character field can take, for create_npc's character option. Call it with no field to list the fields that take a value from a table. Call it with a field to list that field's values, with a description of what each named option does.

field.description: The field to list, from the fields that take a table value.

name: lookup_rule
description: Read the full text of a rule. Your context lists every rule with a brief and shows the important rules in full. Read a rule you only have the brief of before you rely on it.

rule.description: The rule's id, as listed in your context.

name: list_lookups
description: List everything you can look up, each with a short brief: the lookup tools, the rules, and the locations and NPCs in the world. Use it when you are unsure what exists. Then look up the full entry with the matching tool.

name: speak
description: Get the exact words an NPC says. A separate step writes the dialogue from the NPC's personality, accent, and quirks, so give the intent, not the words. The NPC must be at the player character's location. In combat, speak only for a line that changes what the player must decide. Quote the returned dialogue as it is.

intent.description: What the NPC wants to say or achieve in this moment.

replace.description: Set true to rewrite the line already queued for this NPC in this reply, for example to amend it before the next line. Without it, a second call for the same NPC is refused.

name: update_location
description: Change a location's description. Move it on the map by giving x and y, or take it off the map by setting off_map to true. A place inside another cannot be given x or y. Its name stays the same. Leave x, y, and off_map out to keep its position. Use delete_location instead to remove the place from the story.

description.description: The new description of the place, in a sentence or two.

x.description: Kilometers east of the map's center; negative for west. Give x and y together, or neither to leave the place off the map. Only when the place's position relative to others is known; do not use 0 as a default.

y.description: Kilometers north of the map's center; negative for south. Give x and y together. Only when the place's position relative to others is known.

off_map.description: True to take the place off the map, for example when its position is no longer known. It stays in the story and keeps its description. Do not give x or y with it. False by default.

force.description: Set true only to put this place on a point another place already has, as when two places are the same spot. Without it, a point another place already has is refused.

name: discover_location
description: Mark an existing location as discovered: the player character has heard about it in detail, or the story has revealed it. A discovered location appears on the player's map. Moving the player character there discovers it too, so use this for places they learn of without going. When an NPC gives directions, discover only the destination; do not discover the other places the directions name.

name: delete_location
description: Remove a location from the campaign. It is refused while any character is still there; move them first, and refused while places are inside it; remove those first. Notes about the location are kept.

name: hire_hireling
description: Hire a character into a player character's company. The hireling has a rolled sheet like an NPC's and is controlled by the player. Its wage is paid from the employer's gold each new day, and an employer who cannot pay is reported as unpaid. The employer must be a player character who has a location. Give the wage the hireling asks for, or the marketplace's listed wage for a hireling listed there. Leave personality, accent, or quirks out to have them rolled. Names must be unique among locations and characters.

employer.description: The name of the player character who hires them. The wage comes from this character's gold.

wage.description: Gold per day, zero or more.

description.description: Who the hireling is: appearance, role, and what they are good for.

personality.description: Optional. How the hireling carries themselves.

accent.description: Optional. How the hireling sounds when they speak.

quirks.description: Optional. Habits or mannerisms the hireling shows.

name: dismiss_hireling
description: Remove a hireling from its employer's company. It stays where it is and becomes an ordinary NPC. Use this when the story has the hireling leave, for example when its wage went unpaid and it goes, or when it chooses to go. Give the cause in a few words.

cause.description: Why the hireling leaves, in a few words.

name: change_gold
description: Give a character gold from outside a purchase (a gift, a reward, a loan repaid, a loot split), or take it away (a tithe, a bribe, a debt paid to someone else). Use a positive amount to give and a negative amount to take. A take is refused if the character lacks the gold; there is no credit. Give the cause in a few words. Use buy_item for anything bought in a shop, and do not use this to make up gold the story has not earned.

cause.description: Why the gold changes hands, in a few words.

name: place_object
description: Put a world object in a place: a location or a dungeon area. It holds what the story has stocked there, such as gold, an item, or a described thing. Give a short name a character can take it by, such as 'clay jar', and a fuller description in contents. Optionally give gold or an item name. Set hidden when the object is not yet found; a hidden object cannot be seen or taken. Use this only for treasure or objects the story has placed; do not invent them unprompted.

place.description: The location or dungeon area that holds the object.

name.description: A short name to take the object by, such as 'clay jar' or 'chest'. Keep it to one to three words.

contents.description: A description of the object, such as 'a cracked clay jar with nine gold coins inside'.

hidden.description: True if the object is not yet found.

reason.description: Why the object is placed, in a few words.

gold.description: Gold in the object, if any.

item.description: The name of an item in the object, if any.

item_size.description: The size of the item, if one is given. Defaults to normal.

name: take_object
description: A character takes a visible object from the place they are in. Gold goes to that character. An item goes into their inventory, and the take is refused if it does not fit. Use this only when a character acts to take the object.

object.description: The object's description, as the Warden gave it.

reason.description: Why the character takes it, in a few words.

name: update_npc
description: Change an NPC's details. Only the fields you give change; the rest stay as they are. Giving quirks replaces the whole list. Use it when an NPC changes, for example after a shift in attitude or appearance. The player character cannot be changed this way. A story-only NPC has no stats until you give them with character, armor, and attacks; this works once, and it refuses an NPC that already has stats.

description.description: Optional. Who the NPC is now: appearance, role, and what they are doing.

personality.description: Optional. How the NPC carries themselves now.

accent.description: Optional. How the NPC sounds when they speak.

quirks.description: Optional. The NPC's full list of habits or mannerisms, replacing the old list.

armor.description: Optional, for a story-only NPC being given stats. What each hit against them absorbs.

attacks.description: Optional, for a story-only NPC being given stats. The NPC's attacks, each with a name and dice such as '1d8' or '1d6+1d6'.

dice.description: The damage dice, such as '1d8' or '1d6+1d6'.

flags.description: Leave out for a plain attack. The flags the rule set defines for attacks.

name: delete_npc
description: Remove an NPC from the campaign. Use it for a temporary NPC who matters little to the story, such as a passing stranger, a hired guard, or a monster from a fight, once they have left the scene or the encounter they were in has ended. Keep NPCs the story may bring back, and remove an NPC who leaves the story or dies only when they are no longer needed. Notes about them are kept. The player character cannot be removed.

name: update_note
description: Change the text of one of your GM notes, identified by its id. Use it when something you recorded has changed.

note_id.description: The id of the note, as given by add_note or search_notes.

text.description: The corrected fact, written as a complete sentence.

name: delete_note
description: Remove one of your GM notes, identified by its id, once it no longer holds true or matters.

note_id.description: The id of the note, as given by add_note or search_notes.

name: ooc
description: Mark the player's message as out of character: they talk to you as the GM rather than to their character, ask about the rules or the world, or ask for a change outside the story. Call it in place of the other tools for the message. An out-of-character step then replies to the player directly and has all the tools. Set no_narration when the reply needs no story beat after it.

no_narration.description: Set true when the out-of-character reply is the whole response. Leave it false, the default, when the story should move on after the reply, which is then narrated.

name: create_encounter_map
description: Create an encounter map: a grid of cells set in an existing location, where a tactical encounter takes place. Use it before starting an encounter there. Cells are scaled by the rule set's grid.

name.description: A name for the map, unique among maps.

location.description: The name of the existing location the map is set in.

columns.description: How many cells wide the map is, from 1 to 60.

rows.description: How many cells tall the map is, from 1 to 60.

description.description: What the map shows: terrain, cover, hazards, and anything else that matters for tactics.

name: update_encounter_map
description: Change an encounter map: its name, the location it is in, its size, or its description. Refused if the new name is taken or a participant would be left outside the new size.

name.description: The name of the map to change.

columns.description: How many cells wide the map is, from 1 to 60.

rows.description: How many cells tall the map is, from 1 to 60.

new_name.description: A new name for the map. Leave out to keep the current name.

location.description: The name of the location the map is in. Leave out to keep the current location.

name: delete_encounter_map
description: Delete an encounter map. Refused while an encounter is using it.

name.description: The name of the map to delete.

name: start_encounter
description: Start an encounter on an encounter map. Its location becomes the encounter's location. Only one encounter can be in progress at a time. Add participants after starting. The player character and NPCs take turns in the order they join.

map.description: The name of the encounter map to play on.

name: end_encounter
description: End the encounter in progress. Any turn in progress ends with it.

name: add_participant
description: Add a character to the encounter in progress, on a side. Player characters default to the party and NPCs to the foes. The turn order keeps each side together: the party first, then the other sides in the order they first appear. A character who is not at the encounter's location is still added, and the result carries a warning to act on.

name.description: The name of the player character or of an NPC.

side.description: The side the character fights on, such as party or foes. Any name works. Leave it out for the default.

name: remove_participant
description: Take a character out of the encounter in progress. If they are taking their turn, it ends and the next participant's turn follows.

name.description: The name of the participant to remove.

name: place_participant
description: Put a participant on a cell of the encounter map, counted from 0 at the top left: column increases to the right and row increases downward. Moving is limited to the rule set's movement per turn, counted as the number of cells moved in a straight line or diagonal (Chebyshev distance). That limit applies only to the participant whose turn it is; moving anyone else is free. The first placement is free. Use this to move a participant, not to tell the story of how they got there.

name.description: The name of the participant to place.

column.description: The cell's column, from 0 at the left edge.

row.description: The cell's row, from 0 at the top edge.

name: end_turn
description: End the turn of the NPC whose turn it is in the encounter. Call it once the NPC's action is resolved. Player characters end their own turns, so do not use this for them.

name.description: The name of the NPC whose turn is ending.
